# Questions are generated by a Claude Code routine, not the Claude API

Questions are written by a Claude Code routine that runs on the student's own Claude subscription, started over HTTP by a Supabase Edge Function that holds the routine token; the routine writes the Questions straight to Supabase. We chose this over calling the Claude API from the app because the student already pays for a subscription and did not want a second, per-use bill. Subscription logins may only be used inside Claude Code and claude.ai, so the app cannot call Claude directly with them.

## Considered Options

- **Claude API (e.g. Haiku):** instant and fully automatic, but billed separately per use.
- **A self-hosted Claude Code CLI behind the app (the T3 Code pattern):** needs an always-on machine logged into the student's account.
- **Import-only, no AI:** free and private, but the Transcript would produce no Questions.

## Consequences

- Generation is asynchronous: Questions appear minutes after a Lesson is added, not instantly.
- The app works for one student only, since the routine is tied to that student's Claude account.
- The Transcript text travels in the routine's trigger body and is never stored in Supabase. That caps one run at about 65,000 characters; a longer Transcript is split across runs.
- The routine's cloud environment must allow network access to the Supabase host and to the Interactive Review site.
